task1.raw: You are Karen Watkins, an IT administrator at ServiceNow. A new employee, Marcus Li, is starting today and you need to get him fully set up in the system. He is joining the L1 IT Support team as an agent, and he will be based out of the NYC Sales Office. You want his user account created and active, you want him added to his new team so he has the right access from day one, and you want the laptop he is being issued — a Dell XPS 15 — registered to him at his office so the asset records stay clean. You have his contact details, the serial number and cost of the laptop, and you know where he sits and which group he belongs to; the IT assistant should handle the lookups, the account creation, the group membership, and the asset registration end to end.
task1.b1: Hi, this is Karen Watkins, IT Administrator at ServiceNow. We have a new employee, Marcus Li, starting today, and I need him fully onboarded in the system by end of day. Please handle the following end to end, including any necessary lookups: 1) Create an active user account for Marcus Li using his contact details, with his location set to the NYC Sales Office. 2) Add Marcus to the L1 IT Support group so he has agent access to that team from day one. 3) Register his issued laptop — a Dell XPS 15 — as an asset assigned to him, using the serial number and cost on file, and set the asset location to the NYC Sales Office as well. Please complete the account creation, group membership assignment, and asset registration so his records are accurate and he's ready to work today.
task1.ours_t: Marcus Li starts today as an agent on the L1 IT Support team out of the NYC Sales Office, so please get him fully live in ServiceNow using the contact details, laptop serial number, and cost I've got on file: create his user account as active, get him into the L1 IT Support group so his access lines up with how that team is currently structured and assigned, and register his issued Dell XPS 15 to him at the NYC Sales Office in a way that fits cleanly with how that location's asset and hardware records are already organized, since I want everything to slot in without clashing with what's already there for that team and site.

task2.raw: You are Karen Watkins, an administrator at ServiceNow. A new hire, Alex Turner, is starting today on the L2 Service Desk team and you need IT to get him fully set up before he logs in. He'll be working out of a brand-new Denver Remote Office that the company is opening in Denver, USA — so the new site needs to be put on the books before Alex's account is placed there. Alex's account should be active from day one with his work email, phone, and the agent role, and he needs to be added to his new team so incidents can route to him. He's also being issued a new company laptop for the role, and you want that asset on record under his name at the new Denver office. You're juggling several other onboardings today and want this wrapped up cleanly in one pass — efficient, no loose ends.
task2.b1: Hi team, this is Karen Watkins from ServiceNow Administration. I need a complete onboarding setup completed today for a new hire, Alex Turner, who is joining the L2 Service Desk team and starting immediately, so please have everything in place before he logs in. First, create a new location record for the Denver Remote Office, a brand-new site the company is opening in Denver, USA — this needs to exist before Alex's account is linked to it. Next, create Alex Turner's user account as active from day one, including his work email and phone number, with the agent role assigned so he can work incidents. Add him to the L2 Service Desk team/group so incidents can route to him correctly. Also, set his account's location to the new Denver Remote Office. Finally, since Alex is being issued a new company laptop for this role, please create an asset/hardware record for that laptop, assign it to Alex Turner, and set its location to the Denver Remote Office as well. I'm handling several onboardings today, so I'd like this one handled cleanly and completely in a single pass with no loose ends.
task2.ours_t: I'm Karen Watkins, and with everything else moving today I need Alex Turner's start on the L2 Service Desk team to land cleanly against how that team and its open work are currently structured — he's brand new, being issued a company laptop, and based out of the Denver Remote Office that we're standing up in Denver, USA, so that site needs to actually exist and be correctly configured before his record points to it, since he'll be picking up routed incidents right away. Get his account created active from day one with his work email and phone on file, the agent role granted, and him placed into the L2 Service Desk group in a way that fits alongside how the rest of that team is currently set up so routing and assignment behave the way they should, then log the laptop as an asset under his name tied to the Denver Remote Office once that location is in place. I want this whole chain — site, user, group membership, and asset — sitting consistently with what's already on the books so nothing about it looks out of step with the rest of the environment when I move on to my other onboardings.

task3.raw: You are Karen Watkins, an IT administrator. A new agent named Jordan Reed is starting today and you need the ITSM assistant to get him fully onboarded in one go. Jordan will be sitting at the ACME HQ office, and he needs to join the L2 Service Desk team so he can pick up tickets right away. He also needs a laptop issued to him on day one — a Dell Latitude you've already set aside, with the serial sticker on the box, ready to be tagged to him at ACME HQ. Separately, there's an existing database server that's currently owned by someone else and sitting at a different site — you want its ownership transferred over to Jordan and the asset record moved to ACME HQ as part of standing up his desk. You have the serial number of that server on hand. Walk the assistant through everything end-to-end so Jordan is set up — identity, group membership, new laptop, and the server handover — by the time you finish the conversation.
task3.b1: I'm Karen Watkins, an IT administrator, and I need help fully onboarding a new agent, Jordan Reed, who starts today — please handle everything in one session so he's ready to go. First, create Jordan as a new agent/user based at the ACME HQ office location. Add him to the L2 Service Desk group so he can start picking up tickets immediately. Next, issue him a laptop on day one: a Dell Latitude that's already been set aside for him, identified by the serial number on the sticker on the box — please tag/assign that specific asset to Jordan and set its location to ACME HQ. Finally, there's an existing database server asset (I have its serial number on hand) that is currently owned by a different user and located at a different site — please transfer ownership of that server to Jordan and update its location to ACME HQ as part of setting up his desk. By the end, Jordan should have his user identity created, be a member of the L2 Service Desk group, have the new Dell Latitude laptop assigned to him at ACME HQ, and the database server reassigned to him with its location updated to ACME HQ.
task3.ours_t: I'm Karen Watkins, IT admin, and Jordan Reed starts today as a new agent based at ACME HQ, so I need him fully stood up before he can touch anything: get his user record created and situated properly for that site, add him to the L2 Service Desk team so he lines up with how that group's current membership and ticket load are structured, get the Dell Latitude that's already boxed and set aside (serial on the sticker) tagged and assigned to him at ACME HQ, and then handle the trickier piece - there's a database server currently sitting under a different owner at another site that needs to be reassigned to Jordan and its asset record relocated to ACME HQ as part of standing up his desk, so make sure that transfer lines up cleanly with whatever that server is tied to and where things stand for the person giving it up before it lands with Jordan. I've got the server's serial number ready whenever you need it - just walk me through getting all of this settled so he's ready to pick up work right away.

task4.raw: You are Karen Watkins, a ServiceNow ITSM administrator. You've got a small pile of housekeeping to clear for one of your client tenants and you want it all wrapped up in this one session. First, a colleague named Lisa Foley has moved offices — her records still point at her old site and you need her user profile updated so her office location reflects the Globex HQ building. Second, there's an open incident, INC-000013, that has been parked on hold while the caller was supposed to bring their device in; that's now happening, so you want the incident moved off hold and back into active work, and you want its service-level tracking resumed so the clock starts counting again rather than staying paused. Finally, while you're in there, you want the published knowledge article titled 'Bitlocker Recovery Key' attached to that incident as the article being applied to work it — but only if no applied or resolution article is already linked to it; if one is, leave the knowledge linkage alone. Walk the agent through these in whatever order they prefer.
task4.b1: You are Karen Watkins, a ServiceNow ITSM administrator handling a round of housekeeping for one of your client tenants, and you'd like all of the following wrapped up in this one session, in whatever order is convenient. First, update the user profile for your colleague Lisa Foley, whose records still show her old site — change her office location to reflect the Globex HQ building. Second, on incident INC-000013, which has been on hold pending the caller bringing in their device (that's now happening), move the incident off hold and back into active work, and resume its service-level tracking so the SLA clock starts running again instead of staying paused. Third, attach the published knowledge article titled 'Bitlocker Recovery Key' to that same incident as the article being applied to work it, but only if the incident doesn't already have an applied or resolution knowledge article linked — if one is already there, leave the existing knowledge linkage as is.
task4.ours_t: Karen Watkins here — I want to clear a small batch of housekeeping for this client tenant in one pass. Lisa Foley recently relocated, so her user profile needs the office location updated to the Globex HQ building since her record still points at her previous site, and it'd be worth having her line manager and department correctly reflected too if that's already how the rest of her team's profiles are structured, so nothing looks out of step with her group. Separately, INC-000013 has been sitting on hold waiting on the caller bringing their device in, and that's happening now, so it should come off hold and back into active work with its SLA tracking resumed so the clock starts running again instead of staying paused — just worth glancing at how the assignment group and priority line up with similar open tickets right now so it slots back in cleanly rather than landing oddly against current workload. While that incident's open, attach the published 'Bitlocker Recovery Key' knowledge article to it as the one being used to work the issue, but only if there isn't already an applied or resolution article linked — if something's already tied to it, leave that linkage as is.

While that incident is being picked back up, you also want the knowledge article titled 'Printer Jam - Tray 2' formally applied to it so the documented fix is on record against the incident. Work with the assistant to advance the problem, resume work on the linked incident, and get that knowledge article applied to the incident.
